question: Should OpenClaw permanently support this earliest-layer-owned configuration model, including the proposed monotonic exceptions for `tools.allow` and `tools.deny`?
rationale: The choice defines which configuration source has authority over security-sensitive settings and becomes a compatibility contract for hosts adopting the feature; implementation correctness cannot determine the desired policy.

options.title: Approve V1 contract
options.body: Accept the startup-only immutable model and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation and its compatibility proof.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft while narrowing path ownership or changing the tool-policy tightening rules before they become public API.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Leave managed overlay composition outside OpenClaw rather than establishing a permanent core configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Approve V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the startup-only immutable model and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation and its compatibility proof.
